papers.title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
papers.abstract: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

papers.title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
papers.abstract: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schr\"odinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

papers.title: Painlev\'e quadrics and their confluence for the dispersionless Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
papers.abstract: We construct and study a distinguished class of solutions of the dispersionless Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (dKP) equation whose geometry is governed by the first and second Painlev\'e equations. The level surfaces of these solutions correspond to three geometric families of central quadrics, and we determine when their level surfaces degenerate into planes. In the parabolic family parametrised by $\mathrm{P_I}$, degenerate levels occur at the stationary points of the transcendent. For the hyperbolic family parametrised by rational solutions of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$, we show that degenerate levels occur at points where consecutive solutions intersect and we give a precise count of such degeneracies. In the homogeneous elliptic family, the Hastings--McLeod solution of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$ is characterised, up to sign, as the unique non-trivial real pole-free solution with Airy asymptotics whose quadric has no finite degenerate level. Finally, under critical scaling, the quadrics generated by the $n$-th rational Painlev\'e-II solution converge locally, and away from poles, to the parabolic quadrics associated with the Painlev\'e-I tritronqu\'ee solution, with error $O(n^{-1/5})$.

papers.title: Novel lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation
papers.abstract: We apply the generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations to construct second-order two- and three-lump solutions and third-order three-, four-, five-, and six-lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation. We determine the long-time positions and amplitudes of these degenerate lumps and show that their anomalous scattering produces asymptotic amplitude corrections that differ from those in the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation.

papers.title: Multiparameter Quantum Affine Spaces and the Scalene Yang--Baxter Equation
papers.abstract: We construct representation-independent families of solutions of the non-braided scalene Yang--Baxter equation from quadratic noncommutative algebras. Beginning with two anticommuting generators, we obtain a continuous deformation in terms of quantum-plane algebras and extend the construction to an arbitrary number of generators. In the latter case the scalene Yang--Baxter relation fixes the multiparameter exchange matrix to an exact multiplicative form, thereby selecting a distinguished subclass of multiparameter quantum affine spaces. We construct finite-dimensional realizations using singular matrices and finite Heisenberg--Weyl operators, as well as infinite-dimensional realizations in terms of bilateral weighted shifts and multiplicative-shift operators. The explicit realizations are generically weakly purely scalene: their individual constituent operators do not satisfy the ordinary constant non-braided Yang--Baxter equation. For selected finite-dimensional realizations, we additionally establish strong purity by obstructing a generic common meromorphic Yang--Baxter parametrization, even up to consistent invertible local similarities and nonzero scalar rescalings. These results provide a representation-independent algebraic framework for constructing scalene triples and a starting point for investigating their possible applications to quantum integrability.

papers.title: Superregular Breathers in the Sasa--Satsuma Equation: Spectral Conditions and Modulation Instability
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the superregular breathers (SRBs) of the Sasa--Satsuma (SS) equation by combining a Darboux construction with a linear stability calculation. The reduction symmetry of the scalar SS Lax pair makes the fundamental SRB construction degenerate. The paired quasi-Akhmediev branches nevertheless yield second-order SRBs in the focusing sector $n|_{\gamma=0}<0$; neither the defocusing sector nor the focusing sector $n|_{\gamma=0}\geq0$ supports this construction. Linearization about the same plane-wave background gives the modulation-instability gain and, on the admissible branches, reproduces its relation to the group-velocity difference. The carrier wavenumber $b$ enters through the background rather than as a coefficient of the SS equation, and changes the spectral roots and instability interval. In the formal NLS limit, the result reduces to the familiar NLS gain. Numerical evolution of finite-width periodic perturbations produces the predicted second-order profile over the displayed propagation interval.

papers.title: B\"{a}cklund transformations of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation
papers.abstract: In this paper B\"{a}cklund transformations of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation are discussed. The B\"{a}cklund transformations are applied to rational solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation, which are expressed in terms of the generalised Laguerre polynomials and generalised Umemura polynomials. Using appropriate B\"{a}cklund transformations, we derive non-unique solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation in terms of modified Bessel functions. Further it is shown that there are also rational solutions in terms of generalised Umemura polynomials for the same values of the parameters, which are not special cases of the modified Bessel function solutions. The relationship between solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation and solutions of the third Painlev\'{e} equation is also discussed.

papers.title: Collective superintegrable systems from the Guillemin--Sternberg torus action
papers.abstract: We present a novel approach to the superintegrability of collective Hamiltonians invariant under a Hamiltonian action of a compact connected semisimple Lie group, $G$, on a symplectic manifold, $M$. For this purpose, we consider $\mathfrak{H} := \mathcal{J}^*(C^\infty(\mathfrak{g}^*)^G)$ and the centralizer $\mathfrak{F}$ of $\mathfrak{H}$ with respect to the Poisson bracket on $C^\infty(M)$, where $\mathcal{J}: M \to \mathfrak{g}^*$ is the momentum map of the $G$-action. By exploiting a Hamiltonian torus action that goes back to Guillemin and Sternberg [GS,1983], we demonstrate that the functional dimensions of $\mathfrak{H}$ and $\mathfrak{F}$ satisfy the equality $\mathrm{ddim}(\mathfrak{H}) + \mathrm{ddim}(\mathfrak{F}) = \mathrm{dim}(M)$. Together with a non-triviality condition, this ensures that the Abelian Poisson algebra $\mathfrak{H}\subset C^\infty(M)$ represents a superintegrable system, and it also follows that the momentum map of the GS torus action yields action variables for the system. Our work provides new insight into collective superintegrability complementing earlier results of Bolsinov and Jovanovi\'{c}.
